overview.description: Double Briskula is a Balkan Briscola variant in which players hold four cards instead of three and play two cards per trick in two sub-rounds.

history.origins: Derived from the Italian game Briscola, which spread to the Balkan coast during the Venetian and Austro-Hungarian eras. The 'Double' variant is a regional specialization common in Dalmatia and Istria.
timeline: 18th-19th Century: Briscola spreads through the Adriatic trade routes.
Early 20th Century: Regional rules for the 'Double Trick' variant are established in the Balkans.
Modern Era: A staple social game in Dalmatian 'konobas' (taverns).
history.evolution: The game allows for more complex strategies by doubling the number of cards played to a trick, increasing the importance of 'briskule' (trumps) and pointndcard management.
history.cultural: Central to social life in coastal Balkan communities, often played with highndstakes and vocal table talk.

setup.players: 4 players in two partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 40ndcard deck (Standard 52 minus 8s, 9s, 10s). Suits: Coins, Cups, Batons, Swords.
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 4 cards to each player. A single card is turned facendup to indicate the Trump (Briscola) suit.

rules.objective: Score more than 60 points (out of 120 total) by capturing high-value cards in tricks.
rules.gameplay:
1. Two Sub-Rounds: Each player plays one card face-up (Round 1), and then everyone plays a second card (Round 2) to complete the 'Double Trick'.
2. Trump Priority: The highest trump card played in the double trick wins all cards. If no trumps are played, the highest card of the led suit wins.
3. Following Suit: There is NO requirement to follow suit. You may play a trump or any other suit at any time.
keyRules: The winner of a trick draws first from the deck, followed by others clockwise.
Communication: In a partnership, the last person to play for each side often signals their cards to their partner (often using traditional gestures or coded phrases).
Winning the last trick gives you the facendup trump card.

strategy.basic: Keep your high trumps (Ace, Three) for the very end of the game or to capture high-point tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Use the first card of your double trick to 'fish' for an opponent's high trump or to set up your second card to win.
strategy.advanced: Since suit following is not required, use your 'scraps' (non-point cards) to signal to your partner which suits you are strong in without losing points.
tips: The Three is the secondndhighest card (10 points)â€”don't play it unless you are certain to win the trick.
Count the points! Knowing that 61 is the target, track your captured cards to know if you can afford to pass on a risky trick.

engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 40 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and eight ranks per suit (6 through Ace), created by removing all 2s through 5s from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy recognition during gameplay.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit in ascending order: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank determines card strength and eligibility for building sequences.
